# blind-ab-verify — contamination-proof blind A/B loop

A change already landed (new prompt / new skill / two copy variants). The question: **is the new
version actually better, or do I just believe it is?** The moment a human knows which one is "the
new version I wrote", the blind read is dead. This skill turns that judgment into a closed loop:
**each variant is generated by a fully isolated sub-agent that doesn't know which arm it is →
assembled into a de-labeled blind packet (with positive/negative controls + a do-no-harm hard
gate) → you read and score it offline blind → results are back-mapped → a three-part verdict +
a blind-packet artifact.** Who's the new version stays secret to the judge until back-mapping.

- **Stack**: needs an environment that can spawn parallel isolated sub-agents (Claude Code / Agent
  SDK). Arm-generator sub-agents run `model=opus`.
- **Required**: the parallel-agent primitive (it builds on `dispatching-parallel-agents`), plus
  **a human** (you) to do the offline blind read — this is not fully automated.
- **Scope**: only the narrow case "change already landed, judge two versions, and the judgment
  must be a human blind read". It does **not** produce PRDs, design plans, or run live experiments.

## When to use

- A prompt / skill change landed and you want to judge old-vs-new without variant-label contamination.
- Two one-line copy variants that need a blind pick.
- You suspect a prior "new version is better" was your own confirmation bias and want a clean re-check.

**Not for**: adversarial pre-work design/review (that's a debate or a review-gate — those are
"shift-left", before the change); a single-shot subjective compare with no control; a real-traffic
effect experiment (that needs an eng-gated live-RPC run — see the fidelity ceiling).

## The three iron rules (summary — full detail in `SKILL.md`)

1. **Arm isolation** — each arm is a separate sub-agent with no shared context and no variant
   label / hypothesis / expected result in its prompt. Single-agent-does-both = contamination.
2. **Blind-packet assembly** — position-randomized P/Q, a positive control (judge must pick the
   obviously-good one or the round is void), a negative control (does the new version invent new
   bad behavior?), and a **do-no-harm regression group as a one-vote hard gate**.
3. **Four-column blind eval** — winner / shape-correct / no-forcing / no-fabrication, and nothing
   else. The judge never writes "this feels like the new version so…".

Then: back-map P↔arm, produce the results table (marking confounded rows), and a **three-part
verdict** — methodology sound? / claim proven (with honest UNPROVEN fallback)? / net signal —
always stamped with the **fidelity ceiling** (prompt-level ≠ live pipeline).

## Ship rule

New version **doesn't have to win** to ship: a **tie (e.g. 3–3) with zero do-no-harm regression**
is enough (it got the thing it was fixing without making anything worse). But **one do-no-harm
failure blocks ship regardless of how much it won elsewhere** — the hard gate is a one-vote veto.

## How to invoke

Install (see repo root README), then:

```
A/B 验证这个改动，打出来我盲读
盲测一下新旧两版
两版文案哪个好，防止上下文污染
```

## Sample output — see `examples/`

Three sanitized blind-packet examples ship with the skill (real project names generalized, numbers
fuzzed, ids removed):

| example | shows |
|---|---|
| [`examples/blind-packet-reward-surfacing.md`](examples/blind-packet-reward-surfacing.md) | results table + PASSED positive control + the textbook "main lift UNPROVEN at prompt level, escalate to live-RPC" honest fallback |
| [`examples/blind-packet-region-emoji.md`](examples/blind-packet-region-emoji.md) | arm-isolation + version pin + cross-arm constant + manipulation check + explicitly-marked confounded rows + superseding contaminated single-agent rounds |
| [`examples/blind-packet-naturalness.md`](examples/blind-packet-naturalness.md) | four-column blind eval (esp. forced/awkward count) + "tie + do-no-harm not degraded ⇒ ship" + do-no-harm (reward presence held) as a hard gate |

## Required scopes / secrets

None. No Lark scopes, no API key managed by this skill. It orchestrates sub-agents and asks you to
read a packet.

## Known limitations

- **Prompt-level only** — it does NOT run the live multi-agent pipeline. Any claim that depends on
  downstream pipeline behavior is UNPROVEN here and must be escalated to an eng-gated live-RPC run.
  Every verdict must state this ceiling.
- The blind read is **human-in-the-loop** — not fully automated.
- Small-N deterministic spot checks are not rates/percentages; single-locale results don't
  extrapolate to other locales without native review.
